# Lab 12.18: Create a Private CA & Issue a Certificate

## What We Are Going to Do
Create a private certificate authority with Certificate Authority Service and issue a TLS certificate for an internal service.

## Steps

1. **Know the cost.** CA Service bills each CA per month. Delete the CA at the end of the lab.

2. **Enable the API and create a CA pool.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud services enable privateca.googleapis.com
gcloud privateca pools create lab-pool --location=us-central1 --tier=devops</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   The DevOps tier is cheaper and does not store issued certificates, which suits short-lived certificates.

3. **Create and enable a root CA.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud privateca roots create lab-root \
  --pool=lab-pool --location=us-central1 \
  --subject="CN=PCSE Lab Root CA, O=PCSE Lab" \
  --key-algorithm=ec-p256-sha256 \
  --auto-enable</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


4. **Issue a server certificate.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud privateca certificates create \
  --issuer-pool=lab-pool --issuer-location=us-central1 \
  --generate-key --key-output-file=app.key \
  --cert-output-file=app.crt \
  --dns-san=app.lab.internal \
  --use-preset-profile=leaf_server_tls \
  --validity=P30D</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


5. **Inspect it.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">openssl x509 -in app.crt -noout -subject -issuer -dates -ext subjectAltName</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   The issuer is your lab root CA and the certificate is valid for 30 days.

6. **Control who can issue.** Only grant **CA Service Certificate Requester** (`roles/privateca.certificateRequester`) on the pool to the services that need certificates.

7. **Clean up.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud privateca roots disable lab-root --pool=lab-pool --location=us-central1 --quiet
gcloud privateca roots delete lab-root --pool=lab-pool --location=us-central1 \
  --skip-grace-period --ignore-active-certificates --quiet
rm app.key app.crt</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   You can delete the empty pool after the CA is fully deleted.

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| CA keys | Held by Google in Cloud HSM |
| Issued certificate | Signed by your private root |
| DevOps tier | Certificates not stored or listed |
| Issuing rights | Controlled with IAM on the pool |
